attempted_claim: Let p be a prime, let Gamma0 subset P^2 be the fixed smooth conic X^2+Y^2=Z^2 defined over Q and independent of p, let P subset F_p^3 be arbitrary with m=|P|, and let Pi be a set of n=m=N planes in F_p^3 whose dual projective points [a:b:c] all lie on Gamma0, with N <= c_0 p^{3/2} for a fixed small absolute constant c_0>0. Prove or disprove that there exist absolute constants C>0 (allowed to depend on Gamma0 and c_0 but not on p, P, Pi) and delta=1/18 such that every such prime-field configuration satisfies I(P,Pi) <= C N^{3/2-delta}. A complete answer is either a proof of this bound for all sufficiently large primes p and all admissible (P,Pi) via polynomial partitioning with ruled-surface analysis of surfaces fibered by the restricted normals, or an explicit infinite family of admissible prime-field (p,P,Pi) with I(P,Pi)/N^{3/2-delta} unbounded.
claim_type: prove-or-disprove incidence upper bound N^{3/2-delta} under direction restriction
decisive_failure: Proved only a Vinh-based reduction to N<=p^{9/8} and the routine K_{2,3}-free O(N^{3/2}) baseline via Bezout, plus negative small-prime heuristic evidence; the quantitative fibered ruled-surface saving needed for the 1/18 improvement was not established and no disproof family was found.
